BATCH_22_PROCESS_NOTES:
  - HELPER EXTRACT JUSTIFIED ON DUAL-CALLER — verifyTurnstile lived inline in auth.ts since framework bootstrap. With Batch 22 introducing the second caller (storefront's placeOrderAsCustomer), the extract pattern from the banked lessons applied directly: protected → public dual-caller → extract to src/lib/. The auth.ts diff was a clean -14/+1 (inline function deleted, import added, even the env import dropped as no longer referenced). Net code reduction with shared single-source-of-truth gain.
  - FALLBACK SITEKEY PATTERN — checkout-form.tsx uses `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY ?? "1x00000000000000000000AA"` for resilience. The fallback is Cloudflare's documented test sitekey that always passes verification — safe for any env that misconfigures the var. Production deployment doc documents the rotation to a live sitekey + hostname registration.
  - WIDGET LIFECYCLE TRIO — Turnstile widget needs three callbacks to behave correctly: onSuccess (set token), onExpire (clear — Cloudflare tokens expire after 300s), onError (clear — handles transient verification failures). Without all three, the form could submit with a stale/empty token and either bypass Turnstile (if token check is server-only) or fail mysteriously.
  - INLINE DISABLED GATE BEAT FAR-AWAY CONST UPDATE — the `const disabled = placeOrder.isPending || !hydrated;` declaration sat 250+ lines above the button it gated. Rather than modify both the const AND the button line, Batch 22 added the gate inline at the button: `disabled={disabled || state.items.length === 0 || turnstileToken === ""}`. Single Edit, single concern, easier review.
  - ADDITIVE NULLABLE MIGRATION IS THE SIMPLEST COLUMN-ADD — webhookProcessedAt is purely informational (audit + observability), not load-bearing for any query path. Nullable with no backfill means zero downtime, zero edge cases, zero risk. Three-stage backfill from Batch 21c was complex because tenantId was a hard requirement for tenant isolation; this is the opposite shape.
  - SCOUT-VIA-BATCH-EXECUTE PATTERN — every Sonnet dispatch in this batch was preceded by a single ctx_batch_execute call that gathered ALL needed line ranges, file sizes, existing patterns, and grep hits in one round trip. Result: each Sonnet prompt could pre-specify old_string content exactly, allowing 2-4 tool-use dispatches with zero thrash. The V32.1 operational lesson about per-dispatch tool budget held perfectly across 8 consecutive Sonnet calls.
  - VERCEL-PLUGIN AUTO-SUGGESTION HOOKS — fired multiple times on lib/turnstile.ts write, storefront.ts edit, and route.ts edit. ALL skipped per Rule 28 priority order. The observability prompt on webhook route remains a genuinely useful out-of-scope idea — flagged for a future observability batch but project has no logger infra to wire into. 12th consecutive batch this pattern holds (was 11 at end of 21c, +1 this session).
  - DEPLOYMENT GATES CARRIED FORWARD — STATE.md continues to flag the two open ops requirements before staging/prod runtime test of Direction F + Batch 22: (1) APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be set in .env.staging + .env.prod (carried from 21a); (2) both migrations (21c tenantId + 22 webhookProcessedAt) must apply via prisma migrate deploy on each env. Both gates now have a dedicated playbook in docs/deployment-direction-f.md.
